summary.text: A minor of a matrix is the determinant of a smaller square matrix made by deleting some of its rows and columns.
Deleting one row and one column of a square matrix and taking the determinant gives a first minor, and multiplying it by (−1)ⁱ⁺ʲ gives the matching cofactor.
Cofactors are useful for computing both the determinant and the inverse of a square matrix.

facts.label: First minor
facts.value: Determinant left after deleting one row and one column

facts.label: Adjugate
facts.value: The transpose of the cofactor matrix

facts.label: Rank link
facts.value: A matrix of rank r has a nonzero r × r minor

facts.label: Positivity test
facts.value: Leading principal minors test positive definiteness of Hermitian matrices

items.prompt: You delete row 2 and column 3 of a square matrix, then take the determinant of what remains. What is this number called?

options.label: The (2, 3) minor
The (3, 2) cofactor sign
The adjugate of the matrix
The rank of the matrix

items.explain: The minor of the entry in row i, column j is the determinant of the submatrix with that row and column deleted.

items.prompt: You have found a minor and now want the matching cofactor. What do you do with it?

options.label: Transpose it and divide by the determinant
Delete one more row and column from it
Multiply it by a power of negative one set by its row and column
Add the row number and column number to it

items.explain: The cofactor is the minor multiplied by (−1)ⁱ⁺ʲ, negative one raised to the row number plus the column number.

items.prompt: Someone deletes one row and one column from a square matrix, takes determinants, and keeps the results. Which two jobs can this feed?

options.label: Finding the matrix's transpose and its rank
Finding the matrix's determinant and its inverse
Finding the matrix's size and its trace
Finding the matrix's rows and its columns

items.explain: First minors lead to cofactors, which are useful for computing both the determinant and the inverse.

items.prompt: You build a matrix out of all the cofactors of a square matrix, then flip it over its diagonal. What is the result called?

options.label: The minor matrix
The complement matrix
The principal matrix
The adjugate matrix

items.explain: The transpose of the cofactor matrix is the adjugate, also called the classical adjoint.

items.prompt: A real matrix has rank 3. What can be said about its square submatrices?

options.label: Every 3 by 3 minor is nonzero and every larger one is zero
Some 3 by 3 minor is nonzero and every larger minor is zero
Some 4 by 4 minor is nonzero and every 3 by 3 minor is zero
Minors of every size are nonzero

items.explain: For rank r there is at least one nonzero r × r minor, while all larger minors are zero.

items.prompt: A mathematician wants to use minors to check whether a Hermitian matrix is positive definite. Which minors does the test use?

options.label: Minors of order zero
Only the minor from the top corner entry
The leading principal minors
Minors with unrelated rows and columns removed

items.explain: For Hermitian matrices, leading principal minors can test positive definiteness, and principal minors can test positive semidefiniteness.
